text: Java fixed `char` at 16 bits in 1995, when Unicode was believed to fit. Characters above U+FFFF are now stored as two `char` values, a pair called a ___ pair.
explanation: It is a compatibility scar rather than a design. The consequence reaches every program that indexes into a string: `charAt` can return half a character, `substring` can split one, and `length` counts storage rather than content. Languages designed after the 16-bit assumption collapsed — Go, Rust, Swift — chose differently, and had the freedom to because their ecosystems did not yet exist.
